subject: Observability evidence & SIEM export for AcmeCloud private deployment - evidence handback
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <pshah@acmecloud.com>, security@acmecloud.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Observability evidence & SIEM export for AcmeCloud private deployment - evidence handback

Hi Priya / Acme security team,

Following up from last week's call — Acme is preparing to accept Redwood's exported observability evidence for the private deployment (VPC) proof-of-transfer. We want to make this as low-friction as possible while keeping chain-of-custody and auditability intact. Quick summary of what's needed from our side and questions for you: 

- What ingest modalities do you prefer for SIEM intake (Splunk HEC, Syslog over TLS, SFTP pull)? We can support multiple.
- Do you require a signed manifest (SHA256 + timestamp) and a signed receipt on your side?
- Preferred time window for the export (we propose 2028-02-14 22:00 - 2028-02-15 02:00 UTC).
- Any additional PII/PIA redaction requirements we should apply before transfer?

Attached is the draft requirements spreadsheet (acme_obsv_requirements.xlsx) with suggested export formats and retention of hashes.

Proposed approach from Redwood: we prepare a tarball of evidence (logs + traces + metadata), sign the manifest with our internal key, provide a presigned S3 endpoint for a one-time download (or optional push to your Splunk HEC endpoint using mutual TLS). We'll include a short runbook and timestamps.

Please confirm ingest preference and whether the export window above is acceptable. If you prefer, we can also do an online walkthrough with your SecOps team during the handback.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Manager, Customer Security Integrations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_obsv_requirements.xlsx (application/vnd.ms-excel)

From: Priya Shah <pshah@acmecloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Li <mli@secops.io>, security@acmecloud.com
Date: Sat, 11 Feb 2028 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability evidence & SIEM export for AcmeCloud private deployment - evidence handback

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifications from the Acme side: 

- Our preference is Splunk HEC push over mutual TLS for events and traces (HEC token rotation policy is strict), and Syslog over TLS for legacy appliances. SFTP is ok only for bulk archived files where HEC isn't feasible.
- We do require a signed manifest (SHA256) and a signed transfer receipt from Redwood.
- No additional PII redaction required for this transfer; our compliance team will run post-ingest checks.
- The proposed window (2028-02-14 22:00 - 2028-02-15 02:00 UTC) is fine, but SecOps wants the handoff to happen during daylight hours on their side. Can you offer a daytime window (US PST morning / US EST midday)?

Security Ops (Mark) — looping you in to confirm HEC endpoint and any firewall allow-lists we need to provide to Redwood.

Best,
Priya
Priya Shah
Head of Cloud Security, AcmeCloud

---
On Fri, Feb 10, 2028 at 09:15 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Following up from last week's call — Acme is preparing to accept Redwood's exported observability evidence for the private deployment (VPC) proof-of-transfer. ...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Feb 2028 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability evidence & SIEM export for AcmeCloud private deployment - evidence handback

Team — Priya confirmed HEC + syslog preferences and asked for a daytime handoff. Notes and ask: 

- They prefer Splunk HEC push (mutual TLS) for live event/trace ingestion. We should be prepared to fall back to presigned S3/HTTPS pull for archived evidence.
- They require signed manifest + signed transfer receipt. We already have code to generate SHA256 manifests and sign with our key; need ops to produce the receipt endpoint or Docusign flow?
- SecOps wants an allow-list for outbound IPs and the HEC TLS cert fingerprint. We should provide a short allow-list and cert fingerprint prior to the window.

Can Kimber / Jonas prepare:
- a splunk_hec_sample.conf (sample push config) and mutual TLS cert thumbprint
- export_manifest_signed.pdf template and a short runbook text for handoff steps (who executes S3 presign vs HEC push; rollback plan)

Tessa — can you own coordination and sign-off with Acme's SecOps? If so, propose alternate windows (Mon/Tue mornings PST) and book the walkthrough.

Marissa

> On Sat, Feb 11, 2028 at 10:04 AM Priya Shah <pshah@acmecloud.com> wrote:
> > Thanks Marissa — this is helpful...

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Feb 2028 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability evidence & SIEM export for AcmeCloud private deployment - evidence handback

Marissa — quick responses and attached samples.

1) HEC push: we can implement a push job that uses mutual TLS client certs (Rotating certs optional). Attached is splunk_hec_sample.conf — it shows HEC endpoint, token-less mutual TLS handshake (Redwood will present client cert). If Acme requires token-based HEC, we can include token header as well.
2) S3 presigned option: create presigned POST URL with single-download constraint, expiry 4 hours. We will include a signed_manifest.json (SHA256 hashes per file) and produce an export_manifest_signed.pdf confirming the hash and timestamp.
3) Chain-of-custody: propose a signed receipt returned by Acme via a short HTTPS POST to our receipt endpoint (we'll also accept a signed PDF back if they prefer manual sign-off).

Attachments: splunk_hec_sample.conf (text/plain), export_manifest_signed.pdf (application/pdf) [template], runbook_handback.txt (text/plain).

I'll attach the actual cert thumbprint once Jonas generates the staging certs (will do Monday).

Kimberly Park
Senior Product Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: splunk_hec_sample.conf, export_manifest_signed.pdf, runbook_handback.txt

> On Sat, Feb 11, 2028 at 11:30 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Team — Priya confirmed HEC + syslog preferences and asked for a daytime handoff...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <pshah@acmecloud.com>, security@acmecloud.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 16:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability evidence & SIEM export for AcmeCloud private deployment - evidence handback

Hi Priya — thanks for confirming. Below is the final plan and the artifacts we'll hand back during the window. Please review and confirm acceptance so we can trigger the export job.

Final plan (summary):
- Window: 2028-02-15 16:00 - 20:00 PST (that's 2028-02-15 00:00 - 04:00 UTC) — per your daytime request we shifted to a Redwood morning / Acme midday slot.
- Primary ingest: Splunk HEC push over mutual TLS (Redwood initiates). Secondary: presigned S3 single-download for archived ZIP.
- Files included: logs/*.gz, traces/*.jsonl, metrics/*.prom (see manifest).
- Integrity: signed manifest (export_manifest_signed.pdf) + SHA256 per-file (included in evidence_bundle_20280214.tar.gz).
- Receipt: Acme will return a signed HTTPS POST to https://ingest.acmecloud.com/receipt or alternatively upload a signed_receipt.pdf to the presigned S3 reply key.

Attachments included with this message (stubs):
- evidence_bundle_20280214.tar.gz (application/gzip) — contains sample logs and traces (redacted).
- export_manifest_signed.pdf (application/pdf) — manifest with SHA256 + timestamp and Redwood signature placeholder.
- splunk_hec_sample.conf (text/plain) — sample HEC push config.
- acme_obsv_requirements.xlsx (application/vnd.ms-excel) — original requirements doc.

Operational notes / runbook highlights:
1) Pre-window: provide Acme with allowed outbound IPs (we will supply a short list) and the cert thumbprint.
2) During window: Redwood ops will initiate HEC push; monitor for HTTP 200 and our internal receipt generator will post the signed receipt.
3) Post-window: we will keep the evidence bundle for 30 days in cold storage; hashes and logs kept for 1 year per contract.

DocuSign acceptance: I also opened a DocuSign envelope for Acme's written acceptance of the transfer terms — link: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/EX-123456789. Signing will expedite automated receipt generation on both sides.

If that all looks good, please confirm and provide the HEC endpoint + firewall allow-list on your side (Mark). Tessa will schedule the technical walkthrough Tuesday morning PST.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments: evidence_bundle_20280214.tar.gz (application/gzip), export_manifest_signed.pdf (application/pdf), splunk_hec_sample.conf (text/plain), acme_obsv_requirements.xlsx (application/vnd.ms-excel)

From: Priya Shah <pshah@acmecloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Li <mli@secops.io>, security@acmecloud.com, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2028 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability evidence & SIEM export for AcmeCloud private deployment - evidence handback

Marissa / team — confirmed. Acme Security accepts the plan and will provide the HEC endpoint and firewall allow-list by EOD Monday. A few points: 

- Our HEC endpoint: https://hec.ingest.acmecloud.com:8088/services/collector (mutual TLS). We'll send the client cert fingerprint and the contact for the on-call SecOps engineer separately.
- Receipt preference: we'll POST a signed JSON receipt back to your /receipt endpoint; we'll also archive a signed_receipt.pdf in the presigned S3 reply key as fallback.
- DocuSign: signed and returned — thanks for getting that started.

Mark — please confirm the exact port and any additional IDS/IPS rules we should coordinate with Redwood for the push job.

Priya
Head of Cloud Security, AcmeCloud
